Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €12306 spend · 243 purchases
✅ What's Working
• #2 variants systematically outperform #1s across every concept — Summer #2 (2.7x), Split #2 (2.08x), iMessage #2 (3.05x), Catalog #2 (2.41x). Iteration is clearly paying off.
• The unnamed Carousel is the account's silent killer: lowest CPP (€30.44), 3.32x ROAS, 179% CTR — and it's only gotten €396 in spend. Criminal underspend.
• Conversational/native formats win: iMessage #2 (3.05x, €43 CPP) and Video _ General #3 (3.13x, €33 CPP) both convert efficiently despite low budgets.
❌ What's Not Working
• Solitaire is a money bonfire — €2,337 combined spend across #1 and #2, blended ROAS ~1.2x, CPPs north of €68. Highest-spend concept with worst efficiency.
• Heart concepts generate vanity clicks but not revenue: Heart Tag #1 has 191% CTR but 0.59x ROAS (€119 CPP). High engagement, zero purchase intent — likely aspirational scrollers, not buyers.
• Split #1 (0.84x) and Tennis #6 (0.91x) are sub-1x ROAS with meaningful spend. The algorithm kept feeding them and they kept losing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel format: only one exists and it's the best-performing ad. Build carousels for Summer, iMessage, Catalog, and Tennis concepts immediately.
• Tennis creative variants: Tennis #2 (6.36x) and Tennis #5 (5.89x) are the account's highest-ROAS ads but starved of budget. Produce 3-4 new Tennis statics and a Tennis carousel.
• Native/conversational creative: iMessage style + catalog-style layouts consistently deliver sub-€45 CPP. Create more text-overlay, chat-bubble, and multi-product grid formats.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Solitaire entirely — both variants are underwater, €2.3K wasted. No amount of iteration saves a concept this weak.
• Pause Split #1 (0.84x, €84 CPP) and Tennis #6 (0.91x) today. They've had enough spend to prove they don't work.
• Stop running Heart Tag #1 — 0.59x ROAS with the highest CPP in the account (€119). High CTR is a trap, not a signal.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €90 spend · 511 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Last Call" urgency framing is the undisputed winner — "Static _ Last Call #1 - Copy" drives 82 purchases at €0.15 CPP and 387x ROAS; seven Last Call variants all convert profitably across static and video
• Artist-specific and Flemish-dialect hooks crush generic messaging — "Static _ RUBEN" (425x ROAS, 57 purchases) and "Static _ Waar vo #1 - Copy" (596x ROAS, 45 purchases) prove culturally local, personalized copy wins
• "Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy" quietly delivers the best ROAS of any ad with real spend (886x, CPP €0.09) — video urgency is proven but starved of budget at only €3 spend
❌ What's Not Working
• Generic organic reposts flop as paid creative — "Static _ Organic #5" delivers the worst ROAS (97x) and highest CPP (€0.45) in the entire account; lazy repurposing costs you
• Total account spend is ~€89 in 30 days across 20 ads delivering 200x–2000x ROAS — you are catastrophically under-investing in a machine that prints money
• Video is under-allocated despite outperforming — all video ads with spend beat most statics on ROAS yet receive less than 8% of total budget
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3–5 more "Last Call" urgency variants with fresh visuals — countdown timers, sold-out section graphics, final-wave pricing overlays; this angle converts at every spend level
• Create artist-specific statics and videos replicating the "RUBEN" formula — individual artist face + name as the hook consistently outperforms event-generic creative
• Shift significant budget into video urgency — "Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy" at 886x ROAS proves the format works; build a full video urgency series using aftermovie clips, crowd footage, and DJ drops
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting generic organic posts as paid ads — "Static _ Organic #5" is your worst ad by every metric; repurposed social content is not performance creative
• Stop spending €89/month on a 200x+ ROAS funnel — 10x the budget immediately or you are leaving tens of thousands in ticket revenue on the table
• Stop defaulting to static-first budget allocation — video Last Call delivers 4.3x the ROAS of static Last Call but gets one-sixth the spend

❌ What's Not Working
• Every 'Copy 2' variant bombs: 'Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy 2' (€190, 0 results), 'Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' (€104, 0 results), both 'Poll #2 - Copy 2' versions (€120 combined, 0 results). Lazy duplication without meaningful creative changes is burning budget.
• 'General Video #1 - Copy' variants are a disaster across all three instances (€466 for 1 result, plus two more at €71 and €68 with zero results) — the copy/targeting variation clearly breaks whatever made the original work.
• 'Dichtbij #1' and 'De Tijd 2 - Copy' together spent €134 for zero results. The proximity angle and press-authority remix aren't landing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more savings-calculator statics with specific price-point examples (€250K, €350K, €500K homes) — the Berekening and Vergelijking formats are proven winners and deserve fresh iterations, not lazy copies.
• Scale the social-proof angle hard: the Thomas Guenter creative proves real homeowner faces + testimonial numbers convert at the lowest CPR — create a full series with different sellers and savings amounts.
• Invest in original video concepts (not copies): the OG 'General Video #1' scales well — build new video scripts around the empowerment angle, process walkthrough, and 'zero risk' USP.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every 'Copy 2' variant immediately — they're collectively burning €500+ with nearly nothing to show for it. If you want variations, change the actual creative, not just the ad set.
• Shut down all three 'General Video #1 - Copy' instances — €605 spent, 1 result total. The original video works; these clones don't.
• Stop running 'Dichtbij #1' — the proximity/local angle has zero traction at any spend level.

🇧🇪

Belgium

26 ads · €4883 spend · 74 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static split formats with offer messaging dominate: "Static _ Offer #1 - Copy" leads ROAS at 3.26x with €39.85 CPP, and "Static _ Vuelta Split #1" drives highest volume at 17 purchases with 2.46x ROAS.
• Product-focused statics convert efficiently: "Static _ Product Ziris #2" delivers the lowest CPP in the account at €32.96 with 2.80x ROAS, and "Static _ Colors #1" sustains strong ROAS (2.62x) at the highest spend level (€729).
• Clean colorway and split-comparison layouts consistently outperform full-bleed and video formats across every creative family.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video creative is a budget drain: all four Sieben videos average 1.40x ROAS combined, with "Video _ Sieben Split #2" burning €169 for zero purchases and "Video _ Sieben UGC #1" posting an unacceptable €160 CPP.
• Full-frame Vuelta layouts fail everywhere: both instances of "Static _ Vuelta Full #2" return sub-1.15x ROAS and "Static _ Vuelta Full #1" sits at 1.74x—all far below their split-format counterparts.
• Before & After format is a vanity-metric trap: "Static _ HelboF _ Before&After #1" and #2 boast the highest CTRs in the account (130%+ and 163%+) but generated exactly zero purchases between them.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more static split + offer/promo creatives: merge the Offer #1 format (best ROAS) with Ziris, Helbo, and seasonal hooks. This is the proven conversion engine.
• Expand product-beauty statics across the full lineup: Product Ziris #2's €32.96 CPP demands Helbo, Selva Snow, and photochromic lens equivalents immediately.

🇳🇱

Netherlands

4 ads · €253 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Full-frame creative outperforms split layout — "Static _ Vuelta Full #2" hit 3.33x ROAS at €34 CPP vs €87 CPP on the split variant.
• Vuelta cycling-event theming generates engagement across all variants, showing NL audience responds to road cycling context.
• "Static _ Colors #1" pulled the highest relative CTR on minimal spend — colorway diversity as a hook grabs attention even if it hasn't converted yet.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Vuelta Split #1" absorbed 69% of total NL budget (€174) at a losing 1.29x ROAS — split-frame layout is bleeding money without converting efficiently.
• Zero product-benefit messaging across all ads — no prescription ('op sterkte'), no photochromic, no polarized callouts. You're competing with Oakley on vibes alone and losing.
• Total NL spend is only €253 with 3 purchases — sample sizes are dangerously small. No ad has statistical significance, making the entire market read unreliable.
⬆ Double Down On
• Full-frame product hero statics — the Full format proved 2.6x more efficient than Split. Build more single-product, clean-background creatives.
• Lead with the prescription sports glasses angle for NL — it's the #1 differentiator vs Oakley/Decathlon and appears in zero current ads.
• Colorway variety hooks — "Colors #1" shows attention potential. Combine color range with benefit copy (photochromic, polarized) to convert that curiosity.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop feeding the split-frame layout — "Static _ Vuelta Split #1" and #2 have combined €208 spend with €0 efficient return. The format doesn't convert.
• Kill the vibe-only approach. Every ad is product beauty shot with no USP messaging. In NL where brand awareness is near zero, you need reason-to-buy copy, not just aesthetics.

27 ads · €2261 spend · 193 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video XPL04 series is the undisputed engine — all 4 variants (KA #1, KA #2, MG #1, MG #2) deliver ROAS 31x–342x with CPPs under €11. This format clearly resonates.
• Video dominates static across the board — every video ad exceeds 22x ROAS; the top 3 purchase-volume drivers are all video or catalog carousel.
• Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee is the reliable volume workhorse at €558 spend, 37 purchases, 22x ROAS — proving product-feed creative scales well for this brand.
❌ What's Not Working
• French-language static variants are a money pit — Static Barista FR #1 burned €143 for 1 sale (CPP €143), Static Quality FR #2 lost money at 0.76x ROAS, and Barista FR #2 spent €28 with zero purchases.
• High-CTR statics that don't convert — Static iMessage #1 has a wild 221% CTR but zero purchases; it's attracting clickers, not buyers.
• Generic static messaging (General #1, Never #1, Quality FR #2) fails to close — collectively €83 in spend with 0 purchases across three ads.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more XPL04-format videos featuring new single-origin coffees — this explainer/showcase style is the top-performing creative framework by every metric.
• Lean into video-first creative production; the data is unambiguous — video outperforms static on ROAS, CPP, and volume simultaneously.
• Iterate on the two winning static concepts: 'Hold' (73x ROAS) and 'Barista Courses' (63x ROAS) — test new variants, NL/FR splits, and seasonal angles of these proven hooks.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all FR static variants immediately — Barista FR #1, Barista FR #2, Quality FR #2, and General FR #1 collectively spent €270 for 2 purchases. Rebuild French messaging as video only.
• Kill Static iMessage #1 — zero conversions despite highest CTR in the account; the creative attracts curiosity clicks, not buyers.
• Kill Static Never #1 and Static General #1 — both are flatliners with zero signal worth saving.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €588 spend · 7 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Social proof creatives crush it — 'Static _ Review #1' delivered 19.27x ROAS at €10 CPP and 'Static _ Review #2' hit 10.06x ROAS in one instance, proving customer testimonials drive high-intent clicks.
• 'Static _ USvThem #1' comparison format is a money-printer in one ad set — 12.53x ROAS at just €37 CPP, showing direct competitor differentiation resonates hard with Belgian coffee buyers.
• High CTRs across the board (most above 100%) indicate the static creative style and messaging hooks are stopping thumbs effectively.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ Search #1' has burned €73 across two ad sets with zero purchases — the fake search bar concept isn't converting, likely too gimmicky for a premium coffee audience.
• 'Static _ Chat #1' spent €28 across two placements with zero purchases — the chat screenshot format isn't generating trust or purchase intent despite decent CTRs.
• 'Static _ Review #2' at €199 spend is wildly inefficient (1.09x ROAS, €99 CPP) — that specific audience or placement is bleeding cash on what should be a winning concept.
⬆ Double Down On
• Mine more customer reviews and testimonials — the Review format is your highest ROAS concept. Create variants with different reviews, star ratings, and specific product callouts (beans vs. machines).
• Expand the 'Us vs Them' comparison angle — test against supermarket beans, Nespresso pods, and other roasters. The direct comparison mechanic clearly converts price-conscious quality seekers.
• Lean into expertise/authority statics — combine review social proof with your USPs (Rainforest Alliance, 'we test every machine') to build a hybrid trust format.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill both 'Static _ Search #1' variants immediately — €73 wasted, zero signal of purchase intent, the concept is dead.
• Kill 'Static _ Chat #1' — two ad sets, zero purchases, the conversational screenshot format isn't working for this brand.
• Kill the underperforming 'Static _ Review #2' ad set burning €199 at 1.09x ROAS — the creative works elsewhere but this placement/audience is a money pit.

Creative Analysis

12 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €609 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• High engagement signals across the board — CTRs on 'Static _ General #1' (147%), 'Static _ Myth #2' (131%), and 'Static _ General #2' (130%) suggest creatives are stopping thumbs and generating clicks.
• The 'Myth-busting' and 'Us vs Them' angles resonate in Belgium — both frameworks consistently pull above-average CTR, indicating the competitive/educational positioning lands with this audience.
• Static format is generating attention efficiently at low spend levels — the creative concepts themselves are not the primary failure point here.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results across ALL 12 ads with €610 total spend is a catastrophic funnel failure — this is not a creative problem, it's a conversion infrastructure problem. Tracking, landing page, or campaign objective is broken.
• CTRs exceeding 100% (e.g., 'Static _ General #1' at 147%) are anomalous and suggest either broken tracking, bot clicks, or campaign set to an engagement/traffic objective instead of conversions — people click but nothing registers as a result.
• Low-spend variants like 'Static _ General #1' (€3, 0% CTR) and 'Static _ General #2' (€3, 37.5% CTR) never exited learning phase — budget fragmentation across 12 ads starved every single one.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the plumbing first: audit pixel/CAPI, confirm conversion events fire on the BE landing page, and verify campaign objective is set to Conversions or Leads — not Traffic or Engagement. Nothing scales until this is resolved.
• Consolidate budget behind the top 3 engagement performers ('Static _ General #1', 'Static _ Myth #2', 'Static _ USvsTHEM #1') in a single properly-configured conversion campaign to give the algorithm enough signal.
• Create Belgium-specific creative: localized Dutch/French copy referencing Belgian EV incentives, installation regulations, and energy costs — generic NL creative won't convert in a market with different subsidies and grid infrastructure.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the budget fragmentation immediately — 12 ads splitting €610 means ~€50/ad, nowhere near the 50 conversions needed to exit learning phase. Consolidate to 3-4 ads max.
• Kill any campaign running on Traffic or Engagement objective — the sky-high CTRs with zero conversions is the classic symptom of optimizing for the wrong event.
• Kill duplicate ad names running in parallel ('Static _ Myth #1' x2, 'Static _ Myth #2' x2, etc.) — they compete against each other in auction and confuse reporting.

Belgium

✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is the clear workhorse — €17.22/lead across 47 results is strong for real estate lead gen. Investment angle resonates with Belgian audience.
• Investment-focused static creative proves the "investeren" message has legs. High CTR signals across variants (236-339%) suggest the visual and hook combination grabs attention even when sample sizes are tiny.
❌ What's Not Working
• Three of four ads got virtually zero budget (€1-€4) and zero results — "Static _ Investeren," "_ 3," and "_ 4" are either throttled by Meta or lost the auction immediately. No learnings extracted.
• "Static _ Investeren" specifically pulled a 0.00% CTR — the creative is dead on arrival. The hook or visual failed completely.
• The entire ad set is one-dimensional: all static, all investeren. No lifestyle, no second-home, no video, no carousel. You're fishing with one lure in a lake full of different fish.
⬆ Double Down On
• Investment angle with concrete proof points — €17.22 leads prove Belgian investors respond. Push harder with 100% rental guarantee, fossil-free USP, and yield messaging.
• Static format works but needs creative variety — test new visual treatments (aerial Westerschelde shots, interior renders, data-driven layouts) to avoid fatigue on the one winning ad.
• Introduce lifestyle and second-home angles as entirely new campaign lanes — you have zero creative testing outside investeren. The "rust, water, ruimte" positioning is untapped in paid.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• "Static _ Investeren" with 0% CTR — pull it now, it's damaging account quality signals.
• Stop running 4 nearly identical static investment ads against each other. Meta starved 3 of them. Differentiate or consolidate.

• Evocative water/wind imagery + instant form combo is the clear winner — "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" delivers 87 leads at €7.91 each, best efficiency-at-scale in the entire account.
• Visit-oriented CTAs and apartment-specific creatives convert efficiently — "Static _ Visit #2 - Copy" (€10.48 CPR, 23 results) and "Static _ Nieuw_App #1" (€6.74 CPR, 14 results) prove that concrete, action-driven messaging outperforms vague lifestyle.
• Video format shows promise at low cost — "Static _ Video #2" pulls €11.42 CPR with 12 results on modest spend, signaling untapped potential in motion content.
❌ What's Not Working
• Investment-angle creatives are dead on arrival — all three "Investeren" variants (€130 combined) generated exactly zero results. The rational ROI pitch doesn't land cold.
• "Static _ Review _ Form" is burning budget at €47.44 per lead (€949 spent) — social proof alone isn't enough without a compelling visual hook or clear CTA.
• Copy/duplicate variants consistently underperform originals — "Static _ Nieuw_App #1 - Copy" costs 5x more per lead than the original (€35.26 vs €6.74), suggesting the algorithm already optimized to the original audience.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more water/nature atmosphere statics with embedded instant forms — this combination (emotional hook + frictionless conversion) is the proven formula at sub-€10 CPR.
• Create visit-focused creatives with specificity (kijkwoning tours, weekend open days, apartment walkthroughs) — the Visit and Nieuw_App angles both convert under €11.
• Invest in short-form video content (15-30s) showcasing the Westerschelde panorama, the dike village concept, and turnkey interiors — Video #2 signals strong conversion potential that needs budget to prove out.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all "Investeren" variants immediately — zero conversions across three ads and €130 wasted. The investment angle needs a completely different creative treatment if revisited.
• Pause "Static _ Review _ Form" — at €47.44 CPR it's 6x worse than your best performer and draining nearly €1K.
• Stop duplicating winning ads with "-Copy" suffixes — every copy variant underperforms the original. Test genuinely new angles instead.

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €1718 spend · 246 results
✅ What's Working
• 'Naoshima #2' is the efficiency leader at €5.38/result with 83 conversions — the Naoshima creative concept clearly resonates with this audience.
• 'Bauhaus #2' drives the highest absolute volume (70 results, €552 spend) at a respectable €7.89/result — proving Bauhaus imagery has strong pull.
• 'Sommerfeld #2' quietly delivers at €5.88/result with solid CTR (495%) — small spend but very efficient, suggesting untapped scale potential.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Bauhaus #5' is overpaying at €10.94/result — nearly double the best performers — likely a weaker creative variant burning budget.
• 'Bauhaus #4', 'Bauhaus #6', 'Naoshima #1', 'Naoshima #3', and 'Sommerfeld #1' have near-zero spend and zero or one result — Meta's algorithm has already deprioritized them, meaning the creative lost the auction.
• All ads are static images — zero video or carousel formats in the mix, which is a massive missed opportunity for showcasing architectural walkthroughs and coastal lifestyle.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lean hard into the Naoshima visual direction — it combines the best efficiency and volume; create more variants with different angles, interiors, and lifestyle framing.
• Produce more Sommerfeld variants — #2 and #3 both perform well, suggesting this project's aesthetic connects; test different copy hooks and image crops.
• Introduce video and carousel formats — these properties deserve cinematic treatment; architectural walkthroughs, drone coastal shots, and design-detail carousels should outperform static in engagement and lead quality.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all zero-result low-spend variants immediately — Bauhaus #4, Naoshima #1, Naoshima #3, Sommerfeld #1 are dead weight cluttering the ad set.
• Stop running Bauhaus #6 — €20 for 1 result at €20.28/result is unacceptable when other Bauhaus variants do 2-4x better.
• Stop treating every creative series as equal — consolidate budget behind the 3-4 proven winners instead of spreading thin across 12 ads.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2541 spend · 91 results
✅ What's Working
• B2B "4 Momenten #1" is the clear winner — €16.28/result with 23 conversions and highest CTR among high-spend ads; occasion-based framing resonates hard with B2B prospects.
• "Boost" concept delivers consistently across both variants (#1 at €19.65/result, #2 at €22.67/result with 21 results) — benefit-led messaging is the most scalable theme in the account.
• Every single conversion (93 total) comes from B2B-tagged ads — the B2B creative strategy and targeting are clearly dialed in while B2C is producing nothing.
❌ What's Not Working
• Consumer/location-specific ads are dead weight — "Deinze #1" (€63, 0 results, 2.73% CTR) and "Watersportbaan #1" (€59, 0 results, 2.19% CTR) are burning budget with no engagement and no conversions.
• "Geen excuus #1" is the worst B2B ad at €57.31/result — 3.5x more expensive than "4 Momenten #1"; the no-excuse angle doesn't land.
• "Bowl #1" is a vanity trap — sky-high 278.79% CTR but literally zero conversions from €72 spent; clicks with no business outcome.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more occasion/moment-based B2B creative inspired by "4 Momenten" — test specific dayparts (breakfast, lunch, after-workout) as individual ads to fragment the winning concept further.
• Scale the "Boost" concept with fresh visual and copy variants — it carries the most volume at reasonable efficiency; iterate on imagery while keeping the benefit hook.
• Build dedicated B2C retail-driver creative that names Bio-Planet and Delhaize explicitly — current B2C ads have no clear purchase pathway, which explains zero conversions; give people a reason and a place to buy.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all location-specific consumer ads immediately ("Deinze #1", "Watersportbaan #1") — combined €122 spent with zero results and sub-3% CTR; the geo-targeting or creative is fundamentally off.
• Kill "Geen excuus" as a concept — #1 has the worst cost/result in the B2B set and #2 shows no promising signal at €7 spend; the messaging misses.
• Kill "Snel #1" — €41.58/result with only 4 conversions at €166 spend; if you must keep the speed angle, let "Snel #2" earn it with a real test budget.

Other

9 ads · €441 spend · 1 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Instagram Post" is the sole converter (4.98x ROAS at €28 CPP) — proof the audience can buy, just needs the right creative.
• Highest-CTR ads lean into newness and seasonality ("New!! Delivery winter 2026" at 822% CTR, "It's thé time of thé season" at 696%) — urgency and fresh drops drive engagement.
• Event-style framing ("Early bird start of the season days!") sparks curiosity even at minimal spend.
❌ What's Not Working
• The two top spenders ("Instagram-bericht" at €173, "Instagram-bericht: ❤️" at €119) burned €292 with zero purchases — generic boosted posts with no conversion intent.
• No ads have clear CTAs, product pricing, or direct-response structure — everything reads as organic reposts, not ads built to sell.
• €440 total spend yielded 1 purchase — the account is funding engagement, not revenue.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-specific hero ads with price, benefit, and a direct CTA — replicate the structure of the one converting "Instagram Post."
• New arrival / seasonal drop angles — the "winter 2026" and "time of the season" hooks pulled the highest engagement; pair that interest with conversion mechanics.
• Social proof and scarcity — leverage the .be local identity with urgency (limited stock, early-bird pricing) to push engaged browsers into buyers.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting generic "Instagram-bericht" posts with no CTA — they eat budget and produce nothing.
• Stop running ads without purchase-optimized campaign objectives — high CTR with zero sales means the pixel is optimizing for clicks, not buyers.

Belgium

2 ads · €90 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Nothing is working. Both 120239394435940631 and 120239393986810631 have zero tracked results and zero ROAS.
• Abnormally high CTRs (108%+ and 140%+) suggest people are clicking — but the funnel after the click is completely broken. Interest exists, conversion infrastructure does not.
• Low spend (€89 total) means the account is still in learning/testing phase — damage is limited, but learnings are also near-zero.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversion tracking or broken pixel/CAPI setup — both ads show 0 results despite heavy click activity. Money is leaking through a hole in the bucket.
• No discernible creative differentiation between the two ads — both fail identically, suggesting a systemic funnel or tracking issue rather than a creative one.
• Campaign objective likely misaligned — CTR over 100% with 0 results screams traffic or engagement objective with no purchase/lead event firing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix measurement first: verify Meta Pixel, Conversions API, and event setup before spending another euro. Nothing else matters until this is solved.
• Lean into Belgian B2B workwear pain points: team uniformity, safety compliance, branded professional image — build creative around these triggers.
• Create a proper lead-gen funnel: free quote request, sample box offer, or consultation booking — give B2B buyers a low-friction conversion point.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill both live ads immediately. Spending on broken tracking is burning cash with zero data value.
• Kill any campaign using Traffic or Engagement objectives — switch to Leads or Conversions with verified events.

✅ What's Working
• Static formats with direct business angles convert — "Static _ Rip #1" leads at €38.28/result with 15 conversions, and "Static _ Business #3 - Copy" delivers the best CPR at €31.73.
• "Copy" variants consistently outperform originals — "Static _ Business #1 - Copy" pulled 18 results while the original "Static _ Business #1" burned €1265 for zero.
• Low-spend sleeper "Static _ Notes #1" converted at €41.39/result — a strong efficiency signal worth scaling.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire Video Concierge series is dead weight — 4 variants, €290 combined spend, only 2 total results across all of them. Format or angle is wrong.
• Original ad variants without iteration flounder — "Static _ Business #1" (€1265, 0 results) and "Static _ Business #3" (€390, 0 results) prove untested originals waste budget.
• Video overall underperforms statics — "Video _ Talking Head #1" costs €134.27/result, and most video ads returned zero conversions.
⬆ Double Down On
• Iterate more "Rip" and disruptive-hook statics — the rip/interrupt angle is the best cost-per-result in the account by far.
• Create more "Copy" variants of any ad with even a pulse — the data proves iteration on winners beats launching new originals cold.
• Lean into proof-based static formats (notes, reviews, before/after) with refreshed copy — "Static _ Notes #1" hints social proof statics can convert cheaply at scale.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Video Concierge creatives immediately — four variants, near-zero return, the concept is proven dead.
• Kill every original static that has a Copy variant outperforming it — stop funding losers that have already been beaten.

🌐

Other

30 ads · €9436 spend · 161 results
✅ What's Working
• Vottem is the standout project — every format delivers: animatie (€25.56 CPR), video (€32.91), logements (€43.26), apt (€44.76). Consistent sub-€45 results across 4 ads.
• Interior/native creative crushes it: stokerie_int_native at €35.83 CPR with 418% CTR and 16 results is the engagement king. Native lifestyle angles clearly resonate.
• Brugge_penthouse is the volume workhorse — 27 results at €36.68 CPR on highest spend (€990). Proven it can scale.
❌ What's Not Working
• Reels are a money pit: wildebeek_reel (€307.69 CPR, 1 result) and Awans_reel (€234.25, 1 result) burned €542 for 2 leads. Format isn't converting for these projects.
• Charleroi is bleeding: Charleroi_native (€225 CPR, 3 results) and Charleroi_te-huur (€159 CPR, 2 results) spent nearly €1K for 5 leads. Either the audience or the creative is fundamentally broken.
• georges_slideshow spent €211 for literally zero results. The CTA image variants are limping at €73+ CPR. Georges project creative needs a full rethink.
⬆ Double Down On
• Animation format everywhere — Vottem_animatie is the cheapest lead generator (€25.56). Roll out animation creative for Stokerie, Brugge, and West immediately.
• Interior/lifestyle native stills — stokerie_int_native proves that showing the lived-in experience outperforms exterior shots. Replicate this approach for every project with finished interiors.
• Vottem deserves more budget — 4 ads, all performing, 36 total results. This project has proven product-market fit in paid. Feed it.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Reel-format ads for low-awareness projects (wildebeek, Awans). They're generating vanity views, not leads.
• Kill georges_slideshow immediately — zero results, €211 wasted. Slideshow carousel format is dead for this audience.
• Kill Charleroi_native — €225 CPR is 9x worse than Vottem_animatie. Either pivot the creative entirely or cut the project from paid.

30 ads · €4028 spend · 135 results
✅ What's Working
• "Doorstromer #1 - Copy" is the clear champion: 69 results at €14.62 CPR with highest spend — proven scale winner.
• "Alleenstaand #2" delivers strong volume (34 results) at an acceptable €23.14 CPR, second-best performer.
• Original creatives consistently crush V2 versions: "Doorstromer #2 - Copy" (€13.59 CPR) and "Jong Koppel #1" (€6.84 CPR) show originals convert far more efficiently.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single V2 creative is dramatically worse: "Doorstromer V2 #1" burned €951 at €86.41 CPR — nearly 6x worse than the original Copy variant. V2 refresh was a step backward.
• ODD creatives generate sky-high CTRs (329-382%) but almost zero conversions — classic clickbait pattern attracting curiosity clickers who never convert.
• "Algemeen" (General) ads underperform across both versions; broad/untargeted messaging yields €60-136 CPR with negligible volume.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Doorstromer-segment creatives building on the original Copy style — this audience converts at 5-6x better efficiency than General audiences.
• Scale the Jong Koppel angle hard: "Jong Koppel #1" has the best CPR in the account (€6.84) but was starved at only €21 spend — massive untapped potential.
• Create new Alleenstaand variations using the #2 original approach (not V2) — proven segment with 34 results and room to grow.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all V2 creatives immediately — they collectively spent €1,631 for only 19 results (€85.84 avg CPR) vs originals at ~€15 avg CPR. The creative direction failed.
• Kill every ODD ad — €154 total spend, 1 conversion, absurd CTRs that signal engagement-bait with zero purchase intent.

• Zero creative diversity — all three ads are literal copies of the same single static image. No concept testing, no format testing, no angle variation. This is not a strategy, it's a copy-paste.
• ROAS is completely untracked across every ad. You are flying blind with no revenue attribution. €217 spent with zero proof of return.

• Once tracking is fixed, test the veranda lifestyle concept properly with 3-5 genuinely different creatives — different angles, formats, and hooks — not copies of one static.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop duplicating the same static and calling it a test. Three copies of one image is not iteration, it's waste.
• Stop spending without functioning ROAS tracking. Every euro is unaccountable right now.

❌ What's Not Working

• Carousel and GIF variants of the contest concept underperform the simple static visual — "Gif | Wedstrijd" spent €14 with zero results.
• Half the account's ads have barely delivered (€1-€33 spend). Budget is spread too thin across too many creatives instead of concentrating on what works.
⬆ Double Down On
• Static-visual contest campaigns — the "Visual | Wedstrijd" template is proven. Replicate this format for new seasonal or thematic contests immediately.
• Civic-action and volunteer-event creatives — "Schoonmaak - Zwin" engagement suggests citizens respond to participatory content. Build a series around cleanup days, heritage events, and local challenges.
• Short, punchy single-image formats over carousels and GIFs — every piece of evidence in this account says simple static visuals convert best for this audience.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop the IZWVL testimonial format entirely — personal-name + location ads are 5-7x more expensive per result than contests and don't justify continued spend.
• Stop splitting contest budgets across carousel, GIF, and multiple visual variants simultaneously — consolidate behind the proven static format and iterate within it.

9 ads · Meta · last 30 days

🌐

Other

9 ads · €522 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• High engagement signals across every ad — CTRs from 311% to 999% suggest audience resonates strongly with the content, especially the Lokeren store opening post (999% CTR) and the Instagram welkom post (601% CTR).
• Product-focused lingerie posts like 'PrimaDonna San Angel' (442% CTR) and 'Wit of zwart' (419% CTR) clearly generate curiosity and clicks — the audience wants to see the product.
• Event-based ads like 'Feestelijke opening' and 'XXL STOCK SALE' drive engagement at relatively low spend, suggesting strong local community interest.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions on every single ad — €523 total spend with 0 results. This screams broken conversion tracking or wrong campaign objective (likely boosted posts with engagement objective, not conversion campaigns).
• No ROAS measurable anywhere — the pixel/CAPI is either not installed, not firing on purchases, or campaigns are set to engagement/traffic instead of sales.
• Budget is sprayed thin across 9 low-spend boosted posts instead of consolidated into proper conversion-optimized campaigns — no ad is getting enough data to optimize.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product showcase creatives clearly resonate — lean into styled lingerie close-ups with clear CTAs and proper conversion tracking behind them.
• The Lokeren store opening narrative drove the highest spend and CTR — use this local-community angle in proper retargeting funnels for in-store visits and online purchases.
• Event-driven urgency (stock sales, openings) generates clicks cheaply — formalize these into structured promo campaigns with landing pages and tracked conversions.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting posts as a substitute for actual ad campaigns — zero results from €523 is unacceptable regardless of CTR.
• Kill the spray-and-pray approach of 9 tiny-budget ads running simultaneously — consolidate into 2-3 proper CBO campaigns with conversion objectives.
